JUDGEMENT
JUSTICE YOGESH KHANNA, OFFICIATING CHAIRPERSON

This Company Appeal (At)(Ins) No.1175/2026 is filed under Section 61 of
IBC challenging the order dated 19.06.2026 passed by Ld. NCLT, Mumbai
Bench, Mumbai in CP(IB)/640(MB)/2026 whereby in an application under
Section 95 of the Code filed by Respondent No.1, the Adjudicating Authority has
appointed Resolution Professional under Section 97, issued the interim
moratorium under Section 96, and has directed the Resolution Professional to
examine the application, including limitation and invocation of the personal
guarantee and to submit a report under Section 99(I).
2.
It was argued by the learned senior counsel for appellant the Respondent
No.1 has no locus to file the proceedings under Section 95 of the Code as there
was no contract of guarantee executed by the appellant and Respondent No.1
and the personal guarantee was furnished only in favour of the Debenture
Trustee (IDBI Trustiship Services Ltd) for the benefit of all debenture holders and
under the Debenture Trust Deed, the power to declare an event of default,
accelerate, invoke the guarantee and initiate proceedings vest exclusively in the
Debenture Trustee, acting only on the written instructions of the majority
debenture holders representing not less than 75% outstanding debentures.
3.
Respondent No. 1 (IIFL One Value Fund - Series B) is, on the admitted
record of the TDPL Committee of Creditors, only a minority debenture holder -
its voting share is 24.51% (claims as on commencement tabulated at the 20th
CoC Meeting dated 13.06.2026), whereas Rare Asset Reconstruction Ltd. holds

4

65.77% and Renaissance Fiscal Services Pyt. Ltd. 4.49%, the TDPL debentures
having been assigned to Rare ARC (30.03.2024) and to Renaissance
(29.06.2024). Respondent No. 1 thus cannot constitute and has not obtained the
instructions of, the Majority Debenture Holders, and the Debenture Trustee has
neither authorised nor filed the Petition. The invocation and the Petition are
therefore without authority and non-est.
4.
It was argued this very objection was raised before the Ld. Adjudicating
Authority, which by its Order dated 12.06.2026, the Bench recorded that counsel
for the Personal Guarantor had taken it through the stipulations of the
Debenture Trust Deed and contended the petition is not maintainable for non-
compliance with those stipulations and reserved the matter. Yet by the Impugned
Order dated 19.06.2026 the Adjudicating Authority appointed the Resolution
Professional without deciding that threshold question of locus, instead remitting
the issue of “invocation” to the Resolution Professional’s examination.
5.
It was argued the recitals to the Supplementary Debenture Trust Deed
confirm this scheme, wherein* Recital (C) records even the amendment of the
Principal DTD was effected by the Debenture Trustee acting on the instructions
of the Majority Debenture Holders a fortiori, the graver steps of default,
invocation and the initiation of insolvency proceedings could not be taken by a
minority holder acting unilaterally.
6.
The Appellant submits the Adjudicating Authority ought to have
determined the threshold question of locus before setting the Section 99

5

machinery in motion, and the Impugned Order is causing serious and
irreparable prejudice.
7.
Thus the issue raised by the learned senior counsel for the appellant is
whether a minority debenture holder without instructions of the Debenture
Trustee, in the manner as is given in Debenture Trust Deed, could initiate the
proceedings under Section 95 of the Code.
8.
Let us see what the Ld. NCLT has to say on it. The Adjudicating Authority
vide its impugned order dated 19.06.2026 has held as under:-
3.Further, Respondent m h1s capacity as Guarantor, executed
a Personal Guarantee Deed dated 14.l0,2021 m favour of the
Debenture Trustee, namely IDBI Truatecsh1p Services Limited
A copy of the said Personal Guarantee Deed dated 14.10.2021
is annexed hereto and marked as ExJ11bit- V. Thereafter,
Respondent executed another Personal Guarantee Deed dated
12.05.2022 in favour of the Debenture Trustee, IDBI
Trusteeship Services Limited. A copy of the said Personal
Guarantee Deed 1 annexed hereto and marked as Exhibit- NN.
4. It is submitted by the Financial Creditor that a letter dated
23.12.2024 was issued to the Respondent, calling upon the
Respondent to repay the outstanding amount due and payable.
Thereafter, the Financial Creditor invoked the personal
guarantee dated 12.05.2022, executed by the Respondent
pursuant to the terms of the Debenture Trust Deed, vide
invocation notice dated 17.03.2026. A copy of Letter dated
23.12.2024 and a copy of the Notice of Invocation of Guarantee
dated 17.03.2026 are annexed hereto and marked as Exhibit -
EE and Exhibit- E, respectively.
5.Thereafter, the Financial Creditor issued a Demand Notice in
Form B dated 05.05.2026 under Rule 7(1) of the Insolvency and
Bankruptcy
(Application
to
Adjudicating
Authority
for
Insolvency Resolution Process for Personal Guarantors to
Corporate Debtors) Rules, 2019. The Respondent, through its
advocate, replied to the said Demand Notice vide reply dated
20.05.2026. A copy of the Demand Notice in Form B dated
05.05.2026 is annexed hereto and marked as Exhibit-F, and a

6

copy of the reply dated 20.05.2026 is annexed hereto and
marked as Exhibit-Fl.
6. The Financial Creditor submits that the total outstanding
debt as on 31.03.2026 is Rs. 206,42,01,875/- (including
·interest, penal interest and Redemption Premium) from
22.03.201
7. In view of the aforesaid, the present Petition has been filed
on 09.06.2026 under Section 95 of the Insolvency and
Bankruptcy Code, 2016, seeking initiation of the Insolvency
resolution process against the Respondent m his capacity as a
Personal Guarantor to the Corporate Debtor.
8. The matter had come up for consideration on 12.06.2026,
where the following order was passed:
"Heard Learned Counsel for the Petitioner. Counsel for
the Personal Guarantor was also present and has taken
us through certain stipulation in the debenture trustee
and has put forward his point that present petition is not
maintainable as the stipulation provide in the debenture
trustee have not been complied with. Matter is Reserved
for orders"
9. Though the Counsel for Personal Guarantor tried to make his
case for non-maintainability of the Petition, however, the same
cannot be gone into and adjudicated at this stage. In this
regard, we refer to judgement of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, in
Dilip B Jiwrajka Vs. Union of India & Ors. (Writ Petition (Civil)
No. 1281 of 2021) dated 09.11.2023, wherein the constitutional
validity of Sections 94 to 100 of the Code was upheld and, inter
alia, held as follows:
"(i) No judicial adjudication is involved at the stages
envisaged in Section 95 to Section 99 of the !BC;
(ii) The Resolution Professional appointed under Section
97 serves a facilitative role of collating all the facts
relevant to the examination of the application for the
commencement of the insolvency resolution process
which has been preferred under Section 94 or Section 95.
The report to be submitted to the Adjudicating Authority
is recommendatory in nature on whether to accept or
reject the application."
10.Accordmgly, having regard to the facts and circumstances
of the present ca e, and considering that at this stage only the
appointment of a Resolution Professional under Section 97 of
the Code is required, no adjudication of the merits of the matter

7

and contentions raised by the Respondent can be dealt, at this
stage.
9.
Now the learned senior counsel for the appellant has referred to Annexure
H Volume III, a recall notice dated 23.12.2024 by IIFL One Value Fund, Series
B. There are two other similar notice of the same date issued by the Respondent
No.1. Para 3 and 4 of the said notice are quoted as under: -
3. Please. note that upon the occurrence of an Event of Default
under Clause 9.1 of the Deed, the Debenture Trustee is inter
alia entitled to enforce/exercise all our rights incl1!ding but not
limited to the rights under Clause 9.2 of the Deed:
(a) accelerate the redemption of the debentures and
declare that all or part of the debentures, together with
accrued coupon, additional interest (if any), and any
other amounts accrued be immediately due and payable,
whereupon they shall become immediately due and
payable;
(b) enforce or invoke security
(c) invoke the personal guarantee and corporate
guarantee
(d) xxxxx
e) xxx
4. In light of the various Events of Default which are continuing,
pursuant to Clause 11.2 of the Deed. the Debenture Trustee
hereby declares all the amounts in respect of the Facilities to be
due and payable immediately and calls upon the Issuer to
make payment of all such amounts (the '~Amounts Due") in full
immediately and in any event no later than 3 (Three) calendar
days from (and including) the date of this letter by crediting the
Amounts Due in the account mentioned below.
10.
It is argued the action is not initiated by the Debenture Trustee but by an
individual Financial Creditor.
11.
Reference was also made to the Debenture Trustiship Deed dated
22.03.2018 wherein the only exceptional clause is Clause 2.1 as under:-

8

2.1 Settlement of Trust
The Company has appointed the Debenture Trustee as trustee
for the Debenture Holders ir,1 and the Company hereby settles
in trust with the Debenture Trustee, a sum of Rs. 1,00 (Rupees
One Thousand only). The Debenture Trustee hereby confirms
receipt of and accepts the above amount of Rs. 1,000/- (Rupees
One Thousand only) in trust hereby declared and hereby
agrees to act in a fiduciary capacity as trustee for the sole and
exclusive benefit of the Debenture Holders and tts transferees
and assignees from time to time, in accordance with the terms
and conditions of this Deed. The Debenture Trustee in such
capacity as a trustee agrees:
(a) to execute and deliver all documents, agreements,
instruments and certificates contemplated by this Deed
to be executed and delivered by the Debenture Trustee or
as the Debenture Trustee shall deem advisable and in
the best interest of the Debenture Holders;
(b) to take whatever action shall be required to be taken
by the Debenture Trustee by the terms and provisions of
this Deed and / or other Transaction Documents, to
exercise its rights and perform its duties and obligations
under such documents, and enforce rights therein for the
benefit of Debenture Holders;
(c) subject to the terms and provisions of this Deed, to
take such other actions in connection with the foregoing
as the Debenture Holders' Nominee may from time to time
direct.
PROVIDED that before initiating any action or exercising
any right or performing any duty under this Deed or any
of the other Transaction Documents, the Debenture
Trustee shall, unless otherwise provided for in the
Transaction Documents, seek written instructions from
the Debenture Holders' Nominee and only upon receipt of
relevant instructions from the Debenture Holders'
Nominee shall the Debenture Trustee exercise such rights
and perform such duties and obligations referred to
herein.
Notwithstanding
such
requirement
for
instructions ·in writing the Debenture Trustee shall not
take any action inconsistent with the instructions of the
Debenture Holders' Nominee, and in the absence of such
instructions, actions inconsistent with the best interests
of the Debenture Holders.

9

For abundant caution it is clarified that, to the fullest
extent permitted by applicable Laws, the Debenture
Holders shall be entitled to proceed directly against the
Company and/or the Security Providers to enforce the
performance of any of the provisions of this Deed and/or
any other Transaction Document in the event:
(a) no agreement can be reached on the form of
indemnification of the Debenture Trustee within a
reasonable period as required in terms of Clause
6.12(h) of this Deed·
(b) if the Debenture Trustee fails to act on the written
instructions of the Debenture Holder/ Debenture
Holders' Nominee within a reasonable period and
such failure to act is continuing;
(c) if in the reasonable opinion of the Debenture Holders/
Debenture Holders' Nominee, the Debenture Trustee
will only be able to act on the written instructions of
the Debenture Holders by incurring unreasonable
costs and expenses ~- (including its legal and other
expenses); and
(d) the Debenture Trustee or Successor Trustee (as the
case may be) has resigned or is removed and no
Successor Trustee has been appointed in its place.
and the Company and the Debenture Trustee (or
Successor Trustee, as the case may be) (if applicable)
shall be bound to treat the Debenture Holders as the
absolute owner of the Debentures for the purpose of such
enforcement.
12.
It is argued none of the above i.e. (a) to (d) were pleaded in the petition and
none of the conditions (a) to (d) as stated in later portion of Clause 2.1 are
applicable. Further he referred to Clause 9.2(a) (ii) as under: -
9.2 Consequences of an Event of Default
{a) On and at any time after the occurrence of an Event of
Default or the occurrence of any event which, after the notice,
or lapse of time, or both, would constitute an Event of Default,
then, unless such Event of Default at the request of the
Company is expressly waived by the Debenture Trustee
{acting on the instructions of the Debenture Holders' Nominee),
the Debenture Trustee {acting on the instructions of the
Debenture Holders' Nominee) shall be entitled to exercise any
of the powers mentioned below:

10

(i) xxx
(ii)exercise any other right that the Debenture Trustee
and/or Debenture Holders may have under the
Transaction Documents or under the Law;
13.
Further he referred to Schedule 3 of the Debenture Trustee Deed which
reads: -
The following provisions shall apply to the meetings of the
Debenture Holder(s):
1. The Debenture Trustee or the Company may, at anytime,
and the Debenture Trustee shall at the request in writing of the
Holders of Debentures representing not less than 1/10th {One
Tenth) of the Debentures for time being outstanding, convene
a meeting of the Holders of Debentures or the happening of
arry event, which constitutes a breach, default or which in the
opinion of the Debenture Trustee affects the interest of the
Debenture Holders. Art; such meeting shall be held at such
place in the city where the registered office of the Company is
situated or at such other place as the Debenture Trustee shall
determine.

Xxxxx
6(i) A minimum of Debenture Holder(s) holding an aggregate
amount representing not less than 51% (Fifty One Percent) of
the value of the nominal amount of the Debentures for the time
being outstanding, personally present shall be the quorum for
the meeting of the Debenture Holders. Provided however it is
clarified that if any Debenture Holder is a Person fanning part
of the Company's group/ Related Party of the Company and
for any Related Party of the Promoters, the Debentures held by
such Debenture Holder shall not carry any right to vote.
Xxx
21.A meeting of the Debenture Holder(s) shall be entitled to
discuss matters and arrive at decisions in respect of all such
items for which the consent of the Debenture l3⁄4llder(s) would
be required in terms of the Transaction Documents.
22. The powers set out in Clause 21 hereof shall be exercisable
by a resolution passed at a meeting of the Debenture Holder(s)
duly convened and held in accordance with the provisions
herein contained and carried by the Debenture Holder(s) by a
majority representing not less than 75% (seventy Five Percent)

11

or such higher percentage as maybe required under law in
value of the votes cast on such poll.
3.10 Meeting of Debenture Holders
In the event that any meeting of the Debenture Holders is to be
held, the provisions set out in Schedule 3 (Meetings of
Debenture Holders shall be followed with respect to such
meeting.
3.11 Actions by Debenture Holders
As per the terms of the Transaction Documents, in the event
that any instructions/consent is to be provided by the
Debenture Holders or any action is to be taken which requires
the
approval
of
the
Debenture
Holders,
such
instructions/consent/approval shall be obtained from such
number of Debenture Holders representing a specified
percentage of the prescribed therefor in such Transaction
Document. Provided however it is clarified that any Debenture
held by any Person forming part of the Company’s
Group/Affiliates/associate4s/Related Party of the Company
and any Related Party/Affiliates/associates of the Promoters,
the Debentures held by such Debenture Holders shall not carry
any right to vote and also shall not be, in any manner
whatsoever, considered for calculation of any specified
percentage of the Debenture Holders as may be required under
this Deed or under any other Transaction Documents in
relation to any instruction or consent required to be provided
by the Debenture Holders or any action required to be taken
by the Debenture Holders.
14.
Thus it was argued before invoking the personal guarantee the meeting of
debenture holders ought to have been called for and its quorum ought to have
been 51% in value and thereafter a Resolution ought to have been passed in such
meeting for invocation of the guarantee by majority of 75% or more in value,
which was never been done in this case.
15.
The Ld. Counsel for the appellant argued in Dilip B Jiwrajka Vs Union of
India & Ors Writ Petition No.1281/2021, the questions which were before the
Court were whether any debt or whether relationship of debtor and creditor could

12

be examined by the Insolvency Professional at the threshold and it was only in
these two circumstances; those being mixed question of facts and law, the Court
held it cannot be dealt with at this stage and has to be seen at the stage under
Section 100 of IBC.
16.
It is further the submission of the learned senior counsel for the appellant
he is not arguing about merits and rather is challenging the locus of the
Respondent to initiate the proceedings under Section 95 since the appellant has
not given any personal guarantee to the Respondent but has given the personal
guarantee to Debenture Trustee. Hence these proceedings ought not to have
been initiated at the first instance and the issue of locus and limitation can be
very well be looked into at the initial stage itself.
17.
The learned senior counsel for the appellant then referred to the judgement
Pawan Gupta Vs Charm Investments Pvt Ltd & Ors, Company Appeal (AT)
(Insolvency) NO.374/2026 decided on 29.05.2026 to support this view.
18.
Further, the Ld. Sr. Counsel for the appellant referred to the judgement in
Prabhaben Ravjibhai Harkani Vs Bank of Baroda & Ors Company Appeal
(AT)(Insolvency) No. 1002 decided on 7th August, 2026 which held:
“45. The above decision shows that appointment of a Resolution
Professional is not an essential requirement in every case under section 94.
The Adjudicating Authority, where it finds, on the admitted facts and the
applicable law, that the application is not maintainable, it can reject an
application under Section 94 before appointing the RP. The order cannot be
said to be invalid merely because a Resolution Professional was not
appointed. The validity of such an order has to be examined in the facts of
each case.
49. In view of the above findings, we are of the view that the Adjudicating
Authority has rightly rejected the application filed by the Appellant under

13

Section 94 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016. We do not find
any factual or legal infirmity in the Impugned Order dated 21.04.2025
calling for interference by this Appellate Tribunal. Accordingly, the appeal is
dismissed. There is no order as to costs. Pending IA’s if any are also
disposed of.”
19.
To suggest his argument the learned senior counsel for the appellant even
referred to Supplementary Trust Deed dated 24.06.2021 which contains the
following clauses:
“c) The definition and all references to the “Debenture Holders’ Nominee” in
the Principal Debenture Trust Deed shall hereby stand deleted and replaced
and be deemed to mean “Majority Debenture Holders’ (as defined
hereinafter).
e) Any determination under the Debenture Documents including with respect
to the materiality or reasonableness of any matter, proof or the occurrence
of any event, circumstance, change, fact, information, document,
authorization, proceedings, act, omission, claims, breach, default or the
satisfaction of any conditions or otherwise shall be made by the Debenture
Trustee (acting on the instructions of Majority Debenture Holders) which
determination shall be final and binding on the Obligors.”
20.
And to the definition of Majority Debenture Holder as under:-
“Majority Debenture Holders shall mean Debenture Holders holding an
aggregate amount expressing not less than 75% (Seventy five percent) of the
nominal value of the Debentures outstanding for the time being.”
21.
Thus he argued in the recall notice dated 23.12.2024 though it was
mentioned the debenture trustee is enforcing the right to invoke the present
guarantee but in fact it was invoked by the Financial Creditor viz the Respondent
herein and not by the debenture trustee. He further referred to Malvika Hegde
Vs IDBI Trusteeship Services Limited and Another 2025 SCC OnLine NCLAT 422
wherein this Tribunal had dismissed the petition under Section 7 of the IBC
only on the ground it was not filed in accordance with the terms as contained in
the Debenture Trust Deed.

14

22.
Heard
23.
We have also heard the learned senior counsel for the Respondent also
and we are of the considered view the issue of locus and maintainability cannot
be adjudicated prior to the stage of Section 100 of the IBC and our this view is
supported by the law laid down in Dilip B Jiwarajka V. Union of India & Ors
(2024) 5 SCC 435, wherein the Hon’ble Supreme Court held:-
“Para 86.6 No adjudication is involved at the stages envisaged in Section 95
to Section 99 of the IBC” and “no judicial determination takes place until the
adjudicating authority decides under Section 100 whether to accept or reject
the application.”
24.
Further in Bank of Baroda Vs Farooq Ali Khan (2025) SCC OnLine 374 it
was held:-
9. The Adjudicating Authority, by its order dated 16.02.2024, has followed the
procedure envisaged under Sections 95 to 100 of the IBC, and has also relied on
the afore-stated principles in Jiwrajka (supra). It specifically observed that
respondent no. 1’s objections regarding limitation and waiver of the guarantee will
be considered once the resolution professional submits his report. This is the correct
approach as the appointment of a resolution professional at the very threshold is
statutorily mandated under Section 97 of the IBC. As has been held by this Court
in Jiwarajka (Supra) the Adjudicating Authority does not adjudicate any point at
this stage and need not decide jurisdictional questions regarding existence of the
debt before appointing the resolution professional.
25.
In Canara BANK Vs Uma Kumari Singh 2025 SCC OnLine NCLAT 1514 decided
by three judges bench, this Tribunal held:
“Para 9-11. We have heard Counsel for the Parties and after examining the record,
are of the considered opinion that there is an error committed by the Ld. Tribunal
in dismissing the application, in all the three cases, filed by the Bank on the first
the date of hearing on the ground of limitation because it has been concluded by
the Hon’ble Supreme Court in the case of Dilip B Jiwrajka (Supra) that no judicial
adjudication is involved at the stages in Section 95 and 99 of the Code.
10.Thus in view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances the present appeals
succeeds and the impugned order passed in all three appeals are hereby set aside.
The application filed under Section 95 are hereby restored to its original number.
The matter(s) are remanded back to the Learned Tribunal to decide the same in

15

accordance with the law. The parties are directed to appear before the Tribunal on
23.09.2025.
11.Before parting, we would also like to add that the Respondents shall have a
right to raise the issue of limitation when the Tribunal would exercise its
adjudicatory jurisdiction.
26.
In CL Sharma V Bank of Maharashtra 2024 SCVC OnLine NCLAT 279 this
Tribunal held:-
“11.The law declared by the Hon’ble Supreme Court in the above
judgement (Jiwrajka) is very clear. The Adjudicating Authority
should consider the issue pertaining to jurisdictional fact at the stage
of Section 100 and there is no adjudication contemplated at the stage
when RP is appointed under Section 97 sub-section (5). The
conclusion recorded in paragraph 86(iii) clearly lays down the
aforesaid. The submission of the Appellant(s) that applications were
barred by time, ought to have been considered at the time when
Adjudicating Authority appointed the RP, thus, cannot be accepted.
27.
In Central Bank of India Vs Deepen Arun Parekh, this Tribunal held as under:-
36. We are of the considered opinion that Adjudicating Authority committed error
in considering the objection raised by the Respondent on the merits of the
application under Section 95 filed by the Central Bank of India at the stage when
RP was not even appointed. The Adjudicating Authority proceeded to enter into
adjudicatory issues, which can be taken by the Adjudicating Authority only at the
time of hearing of Section 95 application under Section 100, as is now the law
declared by the Hon’ble Supreme Court in Dilip B Jiwrajka’s case, as noted above.
28.
Further in Prabhaben Ravjibhai Harkani Vs Bank of Baroda, Company Appeal
(AT) (Ins) No.1002/2025 decided on 07.08.2026 this Tribunal held:-
This judgement applies to applications filed under Section 94 of the IBC i.e.
applications filed by the debtor itself. It will not apply to applications filed under
Section 95 of the IBC i.e. applications filed by creditors/personal guarantors.
This judgement itself recognizes that different procedures apply to proceeddings
under Section 94 and Section 95.
39. The learned counsel for the appellant has also relied upon the judgement of the
Hon’ble Supreme Court in Di8lip Jiwrajka V Union of India (2024) 5 SCC 435 to
contend that once an application under Section 94 is filed, the Adjudicating
Authority is required to appoint a Resolution Professional before examining the
application on merits. It is, therefore, necessary to consider whether the said
judgment has an application to the facts of the present case.
29.
Thus in view of the law laid down by the Hon’ble Supreme Court and also
three judges bench of this Tribunal, we are not inclined to interfere with

16

impugned order of the Ld. NCLT and dismiss the appeal filed by the appellant as
per settled law viz the adjudicatory process shall start only after the report is
filed by the Resolution Professional per Section 100 of the IBC.
30.

examine the application, including limitation and invocation of the personal
guarantee and to submit a report under Section 99(I).
2.

accelerate, invoke the guarantee and initiate proceedings vest exclusively in the
Debenture Trustee, acting only on the written instructions of the majority
debenture holders representing not less than 75% outstanding debentures.
3.

record of the TDPL Committee of Creditors, only a minority debenture holder -

We have also heard the learned senior counsel for the Respondent also

supported by the law laid down in Dilip B Jiwarajka V. Union of India & Ors
(2024) 5 SCC 435, wherein the Hon’ble Supreme Court held:-
“Para 86.6 No adjudication is involved at the stages envisaged in Section 95
to Section 99 of the IBC” and “no judicial determination takes place until the
adjudicating authority decides under Section 100 whether to accept or reject
the application.”
24.
Further in Bank of Baroda Vs Farooq Ali Khan (2025) SCC OnLine 374 it
was held:-
9. The Adjudicating Authority, by its order dated 16.02.2024, has followed the
procedure envisaged under Sections 95 to 100 of the IBC, and has also relied on
the afore-stated principles in Jiwrajka (supra). It specifically observed that
respondent no. 1’s objections regarding limitation and waiver of the guarantee will
be considered once the resolution professional submits his report. This is the correct
approach as the appointment of a resolution professional at the very threshold is
statutorily mandated under Section 97 of the IBC. As has been held by this Court
in Jiwarajka (Supra) the Adjudicating Authority does not adjudicate any point at
this stage and need not decide jurisdictional questions regarding existence of the
debt before appointing the resolution professional.
25.
In Canara BANK Vs Uma Kumari Singh 2025 SCC OnLine NCLAT 1514 decided
by three judges bench, this Tribunal held:
“Para 9-11. We have heard Counsel for the Parties and after examining the record,
are of the considered opinion that there is an error committed by the Ld. Tribunal
in dismissing the application, in all the three cases, filed by the Bank on the first
the date of hearing on the ground of limitation because it has been concluded by
the Hon’ble Supreme Court in the case of Dilip B Jiwrajka (Supra) that no judicial
adjudication is involved at the stages in Section 95 and 99 of the Code.
10.Thus in view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances the present appeals
succeeds and the impugned order passed in all three appeals are hereby set aside.
The application filed under Section 95 are hereby restored to its original number.
The matter(s) are remanded back to the Learned Tribunal to decide the same in

[PAGE 15]
15

accordance with the law. The parties are directed to appear before the Tribunal on
23.09.2025.
11.Before parting, we would also like to add that the Respondents shall have a
right to raise the issue of limitation when the Tribunal would exercise its
adjudicatory jurisdiction.
26.
In CL Sharma V Bank of Maharashtra 2024 SCVC OnLine NCLAT 279 this
Tribunal held:-
“11.The law declared by the Hon’ble Supreme Court in the above
judgement (Jiwrajka) is very clear. The Adjudicating Authority
should consider the issue pertaining to jurisdictional fact at the stage
of Section 100 and there is no adjudication contemplated at the stage
when RP is appointed under Section 97 sub-section (5). The
conclusion recorded in paragraph 86(iii) clearly lays down the
aforesaid. The submission of the Appellant(s) that applications were
barred by time, ought to have been considered at the time when
Adjudicating Authority appointed the RP, thus, cannot be accepted.
27.
In Central Bank of India Vs Deepen Arun Parekh, this Tribunal held as under:-
36. We are of the considered opinion that Adjudicating Authority committed error
in considering the objection raised by the Respondent on the merits of the
application under Section 95 filed by the Central Bank of India at the stage when
RP was not even appointed. The Adjudicating Authority proceeded to enter into
adjudicatory issues, which can be taken by the Adjudicating Authority only at the
time of hearing of Section 95 application under Section 100, as is now the law
declared by the Hon’ble Supreme Court in Dilip B Jiwrajka’s case, as noted above.
28.
Further in Prabhaben Ravjibhai Harkani Vs Bank of Baroda, Company Appeal
(AT) (Ins) No.1002/2025 decided on 07.08.2026 this Tribunal held:-
This judgement applies to applications filed under Section 94 of the IBC i.e.
applications filed by the debtor itself. It will not apply to applications filed under
Section 95 of the IBC i.e. applications filed by creditors/personal guarantors.
This judgement itself recognizes that different procedures apply to proceeddings
under Section 94 and Section 95.
39. The learned counsel for the appellant has also relied upon the judgement of the
Hon’ble Supreme Court in Di8lip Jiwrajka V Union of India (2024) 5 SCC 435 to
contend that once an application under Section 94 is filed, the Adjudicating
Authority is required to appoint a Resolution Professional before examining the
application on merits. It is, therefore, necessary to consider whether the said
judgment has an application to the facts of the present case.
29.
Thus in view of the law laid down by the Hon’ble Supreme Court and also
three judges bench of this Tribunal, we are not inclined to interfere with

impugned order of the Ld. NCLT and dismiss the appeal filed by the appellant as
per settled law viz the adjudicatory process shall start only after the report is
filed by the Resolution Professional per Section 100 of the IBC.
30.
The appeals are accordingly dismissed. Pending applications are also
disposed of.
